lugworm<tab>lugworms<tab>A hairy marine worm that lives under beach sand. Live bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Lugworm
moth pupa<tab>moth pupae<tab>A moth in the third stage of its development into an adult. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Moth Pupa
pill bug<tab>pill bugs<tab>A small insect covered in a grey protective carapace. Is known to curl up in a ball when agitated. Live bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Pill Bug
crayfish ball<tab>crayfish balls<tab>A ball of crayfish and rye flour paste. Processed bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Crayfish Ball
goby ball<tab>goby balls<tab>A ball of goby and rye flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Goby Ball
bloodworm<tab>bloodworms<tab>A common earthworm that earns its name from the blood red tint of its body. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Bloodworm
rat tail<tab>rat tails<tab>The thin tail of a rat, often carried by young Lalafellin boys as a good-luck charm. Bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Rat Tail
midge basket<tab>midge baskets<tab>A tightly knitted wicker basket filled with a swarm of biting midges. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Midge Basket
crab ball<tab>crab balls<tab>A ball of crabmeat and rye flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Crab Ball

butterworm<tab>butterworms<tab>If allowed to pupate, this bright-yellow larva will transform into a hideous moth which can devour an entire tunic in a single turn of the sun. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Butterworm
bass ball<tab>bass balls<tab>A ball of dark bass and sunset flour paste. Processed bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Bass Ball

spoon worm<tab>spoon worms<tab>Also colorfully known as a “fisherman's member,” the stench of this sea-dwelling creature when sliced up is perfect for attracting hungry fish. Live bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Spoon Worm
syrphid basket<tab>syrphid baskets<tab>A tightly knitted wicker basket filled with a swarm of angry syrphids. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Syrphid Basket
herring ball<tab>herring balls<tab>A ball of Indigo herring and sunset flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Herring Ball
honey worm<tab>honey worms<tab>The honeyfly will lay its eggs in beehives where, upon hatching, the larvae will feed on honey until pupation. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Honey Worm

sand leech<tab>sand leeches<tab>A spineless creature which hides patiently under the desert─ofttimes for several moons─until a larger beast passes nearby. The leech will then attach itself to the new host's leg and proceed to drink deep of the beast's blood until its belly is full, after which it releases itself back to the desert to wait for its next victim. Live bait for dunefishing.<tab>Sand Leech
stem borer<tab>stem borers<tab>This longhorn beetle larva can most commonly be found burrowed deep into the trunks of fallen logs. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Stem Borer

sand gecko<tab>sand geckos<tab>When night falls, thousands of these tiny scalekin can be seen scampering about the Sagolii Desert in search of the beetles on which they dine. Live bait for dunefishing.<tab>Sand Gecko

glowworm<tab>glowworms<tab>It is not known why one end of these vilekin shines bright like a candle. It is, however, known that the light emitted by these creatures makes them a perfect target for hungry fish. Live bait for freshwater and ocean fishing.<tab>Glowworm

rolling stone<tab>rolling stones<tab>When threatened, this tiny desert crustacean will curl itself into a ball which, to the untrained eye, will appear no more than a simple pebble. Live bait for dunefishing.<tab>Rolling Stone

hoverworm<tab>hoverworms<tab>Unlike other vilekin larvae, the hoverworm is not confined to life on the ground. Filling its belly with air allows it to freely ride the thermals over the Sea of Clouds. Live bait for skyfishing.<tab>Hoverworm
fistful of northern krill<tab>fistfuls of northern krill<tab>Microscopic shrimp which inhabit the colder sea currents hailing from the northern seas. Live bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Northern Krill

caddisfly larva<tab>caddisfly larvae<tab>The fact they are extremely difficult to harvest from their underwater homes makes fishing with caddisfly larvae an option for only the most well-to-do anglers. Live bait for freshwater fishing.<tab>Caddisfly Larva

soil creeper<tab>soil creepers<tab>Atypical of common caterpillars, this sand-dwelling species is covered in a rock-like outer skin which serves to prevent the loss of moisture to the hot desert sun. Live bait for dunefishing.<tab>Soil Creeper

balloon bug<tab>balloon bugs<tab>With wings too underdeveloped for flying, this beetle has adopted another method of locomotion about the Sea of Clouds─a second bladder it fills with a noxious lighter-than-air gas. This foul stench is known to attract larger, hungrier creatures. Live bait for skyfishing.<tab>Balloon Bug
chocobo fly<tab>chocobo flies<tab>A freshwater fishing lure made from a chocobo feather. The faint aroma of stable hay brings back memories of a simpler time.<tab>Chocobo Fly
floating minnow<tab>floating minnows<tab>A light plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Especially effective when used to land fish swimming close to the water's surface.<tab>Floating Minnow

brass spoon lure<tab>brass spoon lures<tab>A polished brass lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting fish. Especially effective in lakes.<tab>Brass Spoon Lure

shrimp cage feeder<tab>shrimp cage feeders<tab>A small metal cage packed with a pungent mixture of chopped shrimp. Fish are drawn to the area as pieces of shrimp break off from the cage. Processed bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Shrimp Cage Feeder
crow fly<tab>crow flies<tab>A caddisfly-shaped lure crafted from a crow feather. Recommended for freshwater fly fishing novices.<tab>Crow Fly

silver spoon lure<tab>silver spoon lures<tab>A polished silver lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting fish. Especially effective in lakes.<tab>Silver Spoon Lure
steel jig<tab>steel jigs<tab>The weight of this steel lure allows for casting great distances, such as from coastlines.<tab>Steel Jig
sinking minnow<tab>sinking minnows<tab>A heavy plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Effective in attracting fish from both surface and floor.<tab>Sinking Minnow
snurble fly<tab>snurble flies<tab>A freshwater fishing lure made from a snurble tuft.<tab>Snurble Fly
heavy steel jig<tab>heavy steel jigs<tab>The sheer weight of this steel lure allows for casting tremendous distances, such as from coastlines.<tab>Heavy Steel Jig
spinner<tab>spinners<tab>A metal river lure designed to resemble both a mayfly and a minnow, allowing for use in a variety of different situations.<tab>Spinner

krill cage feeder<tab>krill cage feeders<tab>A small metal cage packed with northern krill. Fish are drawn to the area as krill float off from the cage. Processed bait for ocean fishing.<tab>Krill Cage Feeder

mythril spoon lure<tab>mythril spoon lures<tab>A polished mythril lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting all manner of lake and marsh life.<tab>Mythril Spoon Lure
wildfowl fly<tab>wildfowl flies<tab>A freshwater lure made from a wildfowl feather. Its uncanny resemblance to a mayfly makes it irresistible to vilekin-feeding fish such as trout.<tab>Wildfowl Fly
topwater frog<tab>topwater frogs<tab>A light freshwater lure crafted to resemble a frog. Best suited for larger prey such as pikes and certain trout.<tab>Topwater Frog

rainbow spoon lure<tab>rainbow spoon lures<tab>A shiny blacklip oyster shell lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting all manner of aquatic life. Especially effective in lakes.<tab>Rainbow Spoon Lure
spinnerbait<tab>spinnerbaits<tab>Several small spinners joined together to resemble a school of fish. Especially effective in rivers.<tab>Spinnerbait
streamer<tab>streamers<tab>A freshwater fly designed to sink below the water's surface, and by doing so, attract the larger carnivorous fish living near the floor.<tab>Streamer

yumizuno<tab>yumizuno<tab>A curved man-made lure used traditionally in the Far East, the name means literally “bow horn.” Increases chances of landing a big catch, even when casting from shore.<tab>Yumizuno

Onion Prince<tab>Onion Princes<tab>He would die 4 U. Or possibly cry 4 U. Or most likely make U cry. 4 U.

Use item to acquire the Onion Prince minion.<tab>Onion Prince

Eggplant Knight<tab>Eggplant Knights<tab>His childhood dream to become a wizard was frowned upon by his overbearing father.

Use item to acquire the Eggplant Knight minion.<tab>Eggplant Knight

Garlic Jester<tab>Garlic Jesters<tab>Every breath you take will act as a reminder that your pungent pal is right behind you.

Use item to acquire the Garlic Jester minion.<tab>Garlic Jester

Tomato King<tab>Tomato Kings<tab>Has issued a royal decree for the public defenestration of any and all who mistakenly claim the king is a vegetable.

Use item to acquire the Tomato King minion.<tab>Tomato King

Mandragora Queen<tab>Mandragora Queens<tab>Though wed to the Tomato King in a move to strengthen the bond of houses Tomato and Mandragora, the queen longs to steal away with her one true love─the Eggplant Knight. What will become of this forbidden romance!? Use item to acquire the Mandragora Queen minion and find out!<tab>Mandragora Queen

wind-up onion knight<tab>wind-up onion knights<tab>An accurate representation of the soldiers who once made up the greater portion of the Allagan Imperial Army.

Use item to acquire the wind-up onion knight minion.<tab>Wind-up Onion Knight

treasure box<tab>treasure boxes<tab>It is unknown what manner of spirit possesses this tiny treasure chest, but the fact that it will not hesitate to nip at the fingers of any who try and pry it open is painfully evident.

Use item to acquire the treasure box minion.<tab>Treasure Box

tiny tapir<tab>tiny tapirs<tab>Natives of the New World claim that tapirs grow by devouring the dreams of their unsuspecting owners. And now you know what to expect.

Use item to acquire the tiny tapir minion.<tab>Tiny Tapir

Nana bear<tab>Nana bears<tab>Pundits claim bears to be the deadliest beasts in the realm. They obviously have never stared into this cute cub's nebulous eyes.

Use item to acquire the Nana bear minion.<tab>Nana Bear

miniature minecart<tab>miniature minecarts<tab>Best when ridden in abandoned mines and temples of doom.

Use item to acquire the miniature minecart minion.<tab>Miniature Minecart

nutkin<tab>nutkins<tab>That nutkins are infamous for being shy and timid creatures shows that this brave beastkin comes complete with a pair of iron acorns on him.

Use item to acquire the nutkin minion.<tab>Nutkin

wind-up Minfilia<tab>wind-up Minfiliae<tab>Unlike the real Minfilia, this one actually accompanies you on your adventures.

Use item to acquire the wind-up Minfilia minion.<tab>Wind-up Minfilia

wind-up Thancred<tab>wind-up Thancreds<tab>Two hundred percent more dreamy than previous models.

Use item to acquire the wind-up Thancred minion.<tab>Wind-up Thancred

naughty nanka<tab>naughty nankas<tab>Like its parent, the ninki nanka, this slippery wavekin will breed like a rabbit if left unsupervised.

Use item to acquire the naughty nanka minion.<tab>Naughty Nanka

panda cub<tab>panda cubs<tab>Untrained in arts both martial and magical, but as scrumptiously adorable as chicken glazed in a tangy orange reduction.

Use item to acquire the panda cub minion.<tab>Panda Cub

draught chocobo whistle<tab>draught chocobo whistles<tab>A small hand-carved whistle that emits a unique, high-pitched tone discernible only by a draught chocobo trained from birth to recognize and respond to the sound. Use to summon your personal draught chocobo.<tab>Draught Chocobo Whistle
direwolf whistle<tab>direwolf whistles<tab>A polished bone horn used to summon an Ixal-trained direwolf.<tab>Direwolf Whistle
storm warsteed horn<tab>storm warsteed horns<tab>A hollowed beastkin horn adorned in Maelstrom red that emits a deep bellowing tone which summons your Storm warsteed.<tab>Storm Warsteed Horn

serpent warsteed horn<tab>serpent warsteed horns<tab>A hollowed beastkin horn adorned in Twin Adder yellow that emits a deep bellowing tone which summons your Serpent warsteed.<tab>Serpent Warsteed Horn
flame warsteed horn<tab>flame warsteed horns<tab>A hollowed beastkin horn adorned in Immortal Flames black that emits a deep bellowing tone which summons your Flame warsteed.<tab>Flame Warsteed Horn
Markab whistle<tab>Markab whistle<tab>This tiny whistle emits a shrill tone which can only be heard by Markab, blessed steed of the Lord of Levin.<tab>Markab Whistle
aetheryte pendulum<tab>aetheryte pendulums<tab>A shard of aetheryte which can be attuned to new adventurers, allowing for swift travel to their side in times of need.<tab>Aetheryte Pendulum

bottle of Realm Reborn red<tab>bottles of Realm Reborn red<tab>A special vintage of sparkling red wine prepared by master vintner Byrglaent of Wineport for the Rising, an annual celebration of Eorzea's rebirth.<tab>Realm Reborn Red

magicked prism (meteor survivor)<tab>magicked prisms (meteor survivor)<tab>This peculiar contraption creates illusions by weaving together myriad shades of light. Produces a radiant light that projects images of the lesser moon Dalamud.<tab>Magicked Prism (Meteor Survivor)
pinwheel<tab>pinwheels<tab>A spinning firework popular in the Far East.<tab>Pinwheel

magitek torch (red lotus)<tab>magitek torches (red lotus)<tab>An original creation of the Garlond Ironworks, this handheld device harnesses the power of magitek to emit a sensuous red light.<tab>Magitek Torch (Red Lotus)

skyrocket<tab>skyrockets<tab>This particular variety of firework resembles a comet when ignited. Why it is not then called a skycomet, only the Far Eastern inventor who conceived the item knows.<tab>Skyrocket

flask of lost Allagan roborant<tab>flasks of lost Allagan roborant<tab>An alchemical potion concocted by mad scientists a thousand years dead. Some of the realm's more daring blacksmiths have applied the unnaturally viscous substance to a variety of weapons and found that it heightens the attributes of certain martial artifacts of ancient Allagan design. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.<tab>Lost Allagan Roborant

spool of lost Allagan twine<tab>spools of lost Allagan twine<tab>An alchemical thread woven by mad scientists a thousand years dead. Some of the realm's more daring weavers have applied the unnaturally pliable substance to a variety of vestments and found that it heightens the attributes of certain martial artifacts of ancient Allagan design. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.<tab>Lost Allagan Twine

flask of lost Allagan glaze<tab>flasks of lost Allagan glaze<tab>An alchemical potion concocted by mad scientists a thousand years dead. Some of the realm's more daring goldsmiths have applied the unnaturally illuminated substance to a variety of gems and found that it heightens the attributes of certain martial artifacts of ancient Allagan design. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.<tab>Lost Allagan Glaze

Rowena's token (creation)<tab>Rowena's tokens (creation)<tab>A note of promise received from Rowena for the delivery of Allagan tomestones of creation or poetics. However, due to the House of Splendors changing its policies, it is now worth less than the paper on which it is scribed.<tab>Rowena's Token (Creation)

early model tomestone<tab>early model tomestones<tab>Though considerably different in construction, Garlond Ironworks engineers insist this bulky contraption serves the same purpose as a traditional tomestone, and is merely of an earlier, less efficient design. This particular variety is not as highly sought as it once was, and may no longer be exchanged for other wares.<tab>Early Model Tomestone

the Vegetarian<tab>Vegetarians<tab>Fisher legend has there was once a mighty liopleurodon who, unsatisfied with a diet of Namazu, is said to have set its sights on plumper prey─namely a portly Lalafellin regent with a penchant for skinny dipping in the warm waters near Hells' Lid. However, the fish quickly learned the limits of its maw's gape, and crestfallen, abandoned the king, a crown-shaped scar on its upper lip its only prize. But rather than sulk, this beast from the deep spent the rest of its life devouring creatures far larger than it, and now, five thousand summers later, the descendant of that legendary pioneer polishes off Plainsfolk like they were popotoes, proving once and for all...life truly does find a way.

length of skybuilders' plywood<tab>lengths of skybuilders' plywood<tab>Sturdy enough to support the weight of several large Roegadyn. Until it isn't.<tab>Skybuilders' Plywood

chunk of skybuilders' alloy<tab>chunks of skybuilders' alloy<tab>At this stage, it is anyone's guess what this alloy will become. If it is extremely lucky, it may even end up as a door knocker.<tab>Skybuilders' Alloy

skybuilders' steel plate<tab>skybuilders' steel plates<tab>Unless a skilled blacksmith or armorer can intervene, this steel is doomed to spend eternity as a useless metal square.<tab>Skybuilders' Steel Plate

skybuilders' ingot<tab>skybuilders' ingots<tab>Even the skybuilders themselves are not quite sure what goes into these ingots, although the general consensus is that it is nothing valuable.<tab>Skybuilders' Ingot

circle of skybuilders' leather<tab>circles of skybuilders' leather<tab>Leather made <var 1A 02 /var>for<var 1A 01 /var> skybuilders, not <var 1A 02 /var>from<var 1A 01 /var> them. Apparently.<tab>Skybuilders' Leather
length of skybuilders' rope<tab>lengths of skybuilders' rope<tab>How long is a length of rope? In this particular rope's case, this long.<tab>Skybuilders' Rope

bottle of skybuilders' ink<tab>bottles of skybuilders' ink<tab>Used for writing in ledgers to keep track of who is owed what. Considering the scale of the Ishgardian restoration, it is expected that a fair few bottles will be exhausted before the work is completed.<tab>Skybuilders' Ink

bottle of skybuilders' hemp milk<tab>bottles of skybuilders' hemp milk<tab>By all accounts, this plant-based milk has a pleasant enough taste, though Ishgardian culinarians have yet to succeed in efforts to turn it into cheese.<tab>Skybuilders' Hemp Milk
skybuilders' wain<tab>skybuilders' wains<tab>Surprisingly maneuverable, even when loaded with bricks and such.<tab>Skybuilders' Wain

handful of skybuilders' nails<tab>handfuls of skybuilders' nails<tab>Thankfully, this is a handful of <var 1A 02 /var>metal<var 1A 01 /var> nails, not ones grown from the fingers of the skybuilders themselves. That would be far less pleasant.<tab>Skybuilders' Nails

handful of skybuilders' rivets<tab>handfuls of skybuilders' rivets<tab>Those with a penchant for having little bits of metal sticking out from every surface in sight will be delighted to receive these carefully crafted metal studs.<tab>Skybuilders' Rivets

handful of skybuilders' rings<tab>handfuls of skybuilders' rings<tab>An object without a clear purpose but will “probably come in handy one day,” as hoarders of useless junk are wont to say.<tab>Skybuilders' Rings

bundle of skybuilders' leather straps<tab>bundles of skybuilders' leather straps<tab>Can be attached to the handles of tools to allow them to be hung from belts and so forth, though care should be taken while walking to avoid having them flailing around wildly.<tab>Skybuilders' Leather Straps
bolt of skybuilders' cloth<tab>bolts of skybuilders' cloth<tab>It seems this cloth is destined to become part of a comfortable couch, or perhaps a nice set of drapes.<tab>Skybuilders' Cloth

phial of skybuilders' plant oil<tab>phials of skybuilders' plant oil<tab>Used in the preparation of several varieties of Ishgardian cooking and, on some occasions, as a condiment.<tab>Skybuilders' Plant Oil

portion of skybuilders' uncooked pasta<tab>portions of skybuilders' uncooked pasta<tab>Uncooked pasta that is perfect for eating during construction. If you like uncooked pasta.<tab>Skybuilders' Uncooked Pasta

skybuilders' barrel<tab>skybuilders' barrels<tab>The expression “a barrel of laughs” was never meant to be taken literally, though if it were, one could fit a fair few in this voluminous wooden container.<tab>Skybuilders' Barrel

skybuilders' hammer<tab>skybuilders' hammers<tab>In days to come, this most versatile of tools will become the bane of every nail that dared to stick out. And the occasional thumb.<tab>Skybuilders' Hammer

skybuilders' cooking pot<tab>skybuilders' cooking pots<tab>In times of war, this metallic item of cookware can double as a makeshift helmet, provided the wearer has an unnaturally large head.<tab>Skybuilders' Cooking Pot

skybuilders' candelabra<tab>skybuilders' candelabras<tab>It almost seems a shame to cover this in layers of melted wax, though sadder still would be a candelabra without a candle.<tab>Skybuilders' Candelabra
skybuilders' rug<tab>skybuilders' rugs<tab>The eventual owner of this majestic piece of thick cloth will be as snug as a bug in a rug. Or on a rug, to be precise.<tab>Skybuilders' Rug

skybuilders' broom<tab>skybuilders' brooms<tab>As the saying goes, “A new broom sweeps clean,” though the person wielding said broom is also due at least some of the credit for any increase in cleanliness that may result.<tab>Skybuilders' Broom

handful of skybuilders' charcoal<tab>handfuls of skybuilders' charcoal<tab>The recipients of the other items in your inventory would probably prefer that you refrained from carrying loose pieces of charcoal about your person.<tab>Skybuilders' Charcoal
cup of skybuilders' tea<tab>cups of skybuilders' tea<tab>As is tradition with tea brewed for builders, it contains enough sugar to make the spoon stand on end.<tab>Skybuilders' Tea

skybuilders' pedestal<tab>skybuilders' pedestals<tab>Though one should avoid putting other people on a pedestal, the placement of inanimate objects should not pose any problems.<tab>Skybuilders' Pedestal
skybuilders' crosscut saw<tab>skybuilders' crosscut saws<tab>It is not only double-edged blades that cut both ways.<tab>Skybuilders' Crosscut Saw
skybuilders' counter<tab>skybuilders' counters<tab>Considering that it lacks the ability to count anything whatsoever, “counter” seems to be something of a misnomer.<tab>Skybuilders' Counter

skybuilders' stone<tab>skybuilders' stones<tab>If the time you have spent in Ishgard has taught you anything, it is that the locals <var 1A 02 /var>really<var 1A 01 /var> like stone.<tab>Skybuilders' Stone

pair of skybuilders' longboots<tab>pairs of skybuilders' longboots<tab>Ideal for leaping from scaffold to scaffold as one merrily frolics about the construction site, while others go about their backbreaking labor.<tab>Skybuilders' Longboots

pair of skybuilders' gloves<tab>pairs of skybuilders' gloves<tab>Any Ishgardian with any sense will already own a pair of gloves, but for those who do not, these will be a welcome gift.<tab>Skybuilders' Gloves
bar of skybuilders' soap<tab>bars of skybuilders' soap<tab>Be careful to whom you give this. They may think you are trying to tell them something.<tab>Skybuilders' Soap

skybuilders' all-purpose infusion<tab>skybuilders' all-purpose infusions<tab>Though the recipe states that this mysterious concoction can cure any ailment, one must remember that it will under no circumstances reattach dismembered fingers, which is a remarkably common complaint among the skybuilders.<tab>Skybuilders' All-purpose Infusion
skybuilders' bed<tab>skybuilders' beds<tab>Children who fail to heed the word of their parents will be sent here without any supper.<tab>Skybuilders' Bed

skybuilders' oven<tab>skybuilders' ovens<tab>In many Ishgardian residences, the oven doubles as a means of heating the house, with the occupants finding themselves subconsciously drawn to the kitchen during the colder months. Which is all of them.<tab>Skybuilders' Oven

skybuilders' lamppost<tab>skybuilders' lampposts<tab>Of all the items you have managed to stow about your person, this surely ranks as one of the largest and most cumbersome. Even the most proficient of aetherochemists would be baffled by the unsolved mystery of your impossibly deep pockets.<tab>Skybuilders' Lamppost

skybuilders' brazier<tab>skybuilders' braziers<tab>Not only can this be used for the cooking of various dishes, it also works wonders in the prevention of frostbite, as many residents of the Brume will attest.<tab>Skybuilders' Brazier

set of skybuilders' overalls<tab>sets of skybuilders' overalls<tab>Designed to be worn on top of other layers of clothing to protect them from dust and dirt and provide additional protection against the cold. Since Ishgardians tend to wear several layers of clothing to begin with, these overalls are cut much larger than those worn in warmer climes.<tab>Skybuilders' Overalls

skybuilders' waterproof sheet<tab>skybuilders' waterproof sheets<tab>Serves to keep out not only water, but wind as well, though the cold inevitably finds a way through eventually.<tab>Skybuilders' Waterproof Sheet

phial of skybuilders' alchemic<tab>phials of skybuilders' alchemic<tab>One of many concoctions that serves little purpose on its own, but can be mixed with others for a variety of effects upon consumption, the large majority being some sort of agonizing death.<tab>Skybuilders' Alchemic
pot of skybuilders' stew<tab>pots of skybuilders' stew<tab>One unfortunate rail was left to stew in its own juices after finding its way into the pot. Literally.<tab>Skybuilders' Stew

skybuilders' yew log<tab>skybuilders' yew logs<tab>The distinct lack of trees is one of many problems the first people to settle in Ishgard chose to ignore, making this otherwise commonplace material─sourced from the East Shroud─extremely valuable.<tab>Skybuilders' Yew Log

chunk of skybuilders' iron ore<tab>chunks of skybuilders' iron ore<tab>While this may look much like any other iron ore found in middle La Noscea, there are subtle differences that only an expert in the field will recognize. The name, for one, is considerably longer.<tab>Skybuilders' Iron Ore

pinch of skybuilders' fine sand<tab>pinches of skybuilders' fine sand<tab>This sand gathered in central Thanalan is not only fine, but extremely well-behaved, choosing to stay in one closely knit lump while jostling alongside the rest of your possessions.<tab>Skybuilders' Fine Sand

tuft of skybuilders' hemp<tab>tufts of skybuilders' hemp<tab>Though this hardy plant can grow almost anywhere, the snow-blasted precipices of Ishgard have so far proven too steep a challenge for it to overcome. This particular specimen was harvested in lower La Noscea, an environment far more conducive to plant life─or any sort of life, for that matter.<tab>Skybuilders' Hemp
skybuilders' ash log<tab>skybuilders' ash logs<tab>Ash! A-Ah! Savior of the Firmament!♪<tab>Skybuilders' Ash Log

pinch of skybuilders' rock salt<tab>pinches of skybuilders' rock salt<tab>Although upper La Noscea seems rather a distant location from which to source something as simple as salt, the Ishgardians are nothing if not particular in their tastes.<tab>Skybuilders' Rock Salt

chunk of skybuilders' electrum ore<tab>chunks of skybuilders' electrum ore<tab>The electrum ore found in upper La Noscea is believed to be far better suited to the skybuilders' needs than any other variety. Were anyone to ask them why, they would, in most cases be met with a response along the line of, “Because it just is.”<tab>Skybuilders' Electrum Ore

pinch of skybuilders' iron sand<tab>pinches of skybuilders' iron sand<tab>The tradition of measuring powdered substances in units of “pinches” has been the cause of many arguments, largely due to differences in finger size between the various races. Folk in eastern Thanalan, where this sample was gathered, have been known to ask Lalafells to measure when selling, and Roegadyn when buying, for obvious reasons.<tab>Skybuilders' Iron Sand

clump of skybuilders' flax<tab>clumps of skybuilders' flax<tab>It is a well known fact among botanists that the flax in the South Shroud is superior to every other kind, for reasons far too complicated and boring for anyone else to care about.<tab>Skybuilders' Flax

bottle of skybuilders' spring water<tab>bottles of skybuilders' spring water<tab>Having only traveled the relatively short distance from the Coerthas central highlands to Ishgard, this spring water is still remarkably fresh, though the icy chill threatens to freeze it inside the bottle.<tab>Skybuilders' Spring Water

skybuilders' camphorwood log<tab>skybuilders' camphorwood logs<tab>Few members of the mortal races are equipped to make the perilous journey to the Churning Mists, and those who do normally hope to have more than a log or two to show for their troubles.<tab>Skybuilders' Camphorwood Log

bundle of skybuilders' straw<tab>bundles of skybuilders' straw<tab>Why the skybuilders would specify that their straw be brought from the Dravanian forelands is anyone's guess. Perhaps the smell helps their chocobos sleep more peacefully?<tab>Skybuilders' Straw

chunk of skybuilders' hardsilver ore<tab>chunks of skybuilders' hardsilver ore<tab>The time spent mining this ore in the Dravanian hinterlands would perhaps have seemed less arduous if you had the faintest idea how the skybuilders plan to use it.<tab>Skybuilders' Hardsilver Ore

pinch of skybuilders' mythrite sand<tab>pinches of skybuilders' mythrite sand<tab>You have a sneaking suspicion that you may have lost some of the sand during the return journey from the Sea of Clouds, though the amount you have in your possession should still suffice.<tab>Skybuilders' Mythrite Sand

basket of skybuilders' tea leaves<tab>baskets of skybuilders' tea leaves<tab>The thought of happy skybuilders drinking delicious tea was the only motivation you needed as you risked life and limb gathering these leaves in the Sea of Clouds.<tab>Skybuilders' Tea Leaves

bottle of skybuilders' Dravanian spring water<tab>bottles of skybuilders' Dravanian spring water<tab>There are easier places to collect spring water than the Dravanian forelands, though it seems your personal safety is not especially high on the skybuilders' list of concerns.<tab>Skybuilders' Dravanian Spring Water

skybuilders' urunday log<tab>skybuilders' urunday logs<tab>Compared to most places in Gyr Abania, the Peaks has more than its fair share of trees, so who would object to you taking a few logs? Bloodthirsty Qiqirn and rampaging ruud suuds, that's who. Or perhaps they just see you as an easy meal?<tab>Skybuilders' Urunday Log

chunk of skybuilders' nightsteel ore<tab>chunks of skybuilders' nightsteel ore<tab>The Ruby Sea is not especially well known as a prime location for mining, though those who are nautically minded can uncover all sorts of rare and unique treasures. Whether the skybuilders choose to turn this into fine jewelry or something more mundane, like a tea strainer, remains to be seen.<tab>Skybuilders' Nightsteel Ore

skybuilders' adder<tab>skybuilders' adders<tab>Venomous snakes are something of a rarity in Ishgard, so the skybuilders have ordered that some be delivered from the Azim Steppe to help improve morale. Workers displaying a lack of enthusiasm will be given some time in “the pit” to rediscover their commitment to the cause.<tab>Skybuilders' Adder

chunk of skybuilders' molybdenum ore<tab>chunks of skybuilders' molybdenum ore<tab>While the Lochs are better known as a source of salt, the rich veins of ore are drawing in miners from far and wide.<tab>Skybuilders' Molybdenum Ore

clump of skybuilders' horsetail<tab>clumps of skybuilders' horsetail<tab>Yanxia is rich in both flora and fauna, and horsetail forms a major part of the diet of many grazing creatures.<tab>Skybuilders' Horsetail

pinch of skybuilders' Ala Mhigan rock salt<tab>pinches of skybuilders' Ala Mhigan rock salt<tab>When an Ishgardian culinarian stated that her latest dish needed a pinch of salt, the skybuilders sought out the very best, though perhaps more than a single pinch would be required to make the lengthy journey to the Lochs worthwhile.<tab>Skybuilders' Ala Mhigan Rock Salt

bottle of skybuilders' Ruby Sea water<tab>bottles of skybuilders' Ruby Sea water<tab>While water from the Ruby Sea may not sound particularly appealing, this was actually brought from a small freshwater spring on one of the surrounding islands. Drinking this is unlikely to result in life-threatening dehydration.<tab>Skybuilders' Ruby Sea Water

pinch of skybuilders' durium sand<tab>pinches of skybuilders' durium sand<tab>A pinch of anything tends not to be an awful lot, though this particular sand from the Azim Steppe is apparently worth more than its weight in gold.<tab>Skybuilders' Durium Sand

skybuilders' vine<tab>skybuilders' vines<tab>Quite why a particular type of vine that can only be found in the Azim Steppe is necessary to the skybuilders' plans has yet to be explained. Perhaps they are planning to surprise you with a work of surpassing genius? Or perhaps not.<tab>Skybuilders' Vine

skybuilders' white ash log<tab>skybuilders' white ash logs<tab>Obviously, none of the skybuilders has even heard of the Rak'tika Greatwood, though the specific qualities they seek in their timber can most easily be found in the white ash trees that grow there.<tab>Skybuilders' White Ash Log

chunk of skybuilders' reef rock<tab>chunks of skybuilders' reef rock<tab>If a porous rock from the bottom of the ocean is required in the rebuilding of Ishgard, then so be it. Your job is to mine, not question the reasoning behind such dubious demands.<tab>Skybuilders' Reef Rock

chunk of skybuilders' truegold ore<tab>chunks of skybuilders' truegold ore<tab>Why submit a boring chunk of gold ore when you can bring one all the way from Il Mheg instead?<tab>Skybuilders' Truegold Ore

skybuilders' cotton boll<tab>skybuilders' cotton bolls<tab>This cotton must be very special indeed for you to bring it all the way from Lakeland in the First. You can only hope that the skybuilders appreciate you going the extra malm. And traveling to another world.<tab>Skybuilders' Cotton Boll

skybuilders' dawn lizard<tab>skybuilders' dawn lizards<tab>One day, this poor lizard is chasing other, smaller scurrying creatures across the desert plains of Amh Araeng, and the next, it is being transported to another world and dragged lashing and kicking to Ishgard. The chances of the cold-blooded scalekin being content in its frozen new surroundings are slim at best, and you can only hope that the skybuilders are grateful to you for supplying a miserable and motionless lizard.<tab>Skybuilders' Dawn Lizard

sheaf of skybuilders' wheat<tab>sheaves of skybuilders' wheat<tab>Were the other contributors to hear that you traveled to Amh Araeng in the First simply to procure wheat, they would think you are just trying to show off.<tab>Skybuilders' Wheat

pinch of skybuilders' truegold sand<tab>pinches of skybuilders' truegold sand<tab>The isle of Kholusia is known by the inhabitants of Norvrandt to have the very finest of gold sand. Whether this is up to the impossibly high standards of the skybuilders will only become apparent when it is submitted for inspection.<tab>Skybuilders' Truegold Sand

bottle of skybuilders' highland spring water<tab>bottles of skybuilders' highland spring water<tab>Any water gathered from Il Mheg is likely to have been enchanted by either the pixies or the Fuath, though that is a problem for the skybuilders, not you, to worry about.<tab>Skybuilders' Highland Spring Water

lump of skybuilders' resin<tab>lumps of skybuilders' resin<tab>Thankfully, the resin appears to have suffered no ill effects during your return from the Rak'tika Greatwood, meaning that it is still a gelatinous blob with seemingly no practical application whatsoever.<tab>Skybuilders' Resin

grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' log<tab>grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' logs<tab>As the skybuilders prefer to use wooden planks of standardized dimensions, this log is already cut to be exactly the length they require, to minimize the carpenters' workload. lump of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' hardened sap<tab>lumps of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' hardened sap<tab>Although the practical applications of a piece of hardened sap are somewhat unclear, it is at least considerably less sticky than unhardened sap, which helps to keep it free of impurities such as loose hairs, bits of pocket fluff, and so on.

sheaf of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wheat<tab>sheaves of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wheat<tab>What about this wheat makes it artisanal? grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cotton boll<tab>grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cotton bolls<tab>To the untrained eye, this may appear to be no different from any other cotton boll. Those with <var 1A 02 /var>trained<var 1A 01 /var> eyes, however, will notice that it is pink, not the usual white.

grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' dawn lizard<tab>grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' dawn lizards<tab>Those wondering what separates this from a non-artisanal dawn lizard need only observe the way it devours its prey. Used in expert crafting recipes.<tab>Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Dawn Lizard

chunk of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone<tab>chunks of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone<tab>Believed to be a piece of fossilized cloud.

chunk of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' rock salt<tab>chunks of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' rock salt<tab>It seems there are almost as many varieties of rock salt as there are varieties of rock, if the skybuilders' somewhat arbitrary system of assigning names is to be believed.

bottle of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' spring water<tab>bottles of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' spring water<tab>Rather than simply being free of impurities, this water actually possesses the ability to preemptively destroy any impurities that dare to come near it. chunk of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' jade<tab>chunks of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' jade<tab>In the Brume, to be “jaded” means to have a large piece of jade thrown at the back of one's head. Thankfully, the prohibitive pricing of this precious substance means that such incidents are rare.

grade 2 skybuilders' cloudskipper<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' cloudskippers<tab>True to its name, this rare species spends its entire life in the firmament (the actual firmament, not the place in Ishgard) where it skips from cloud to cloud. ※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Cloudskipper

grade 2 skybuilders' meditator<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' meditators<tab>Like all meditators, this particular variety is capable of surviving out of water. The reason for its superior grading appears to be its ability to get back into water afterwards, which many of its brethren sadly lack.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Meditator

grade 2 skybuilders' coeurlfish<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' coeurlfish<tab>Coeurlfish fall into the category of species that anglers would rather not have thrashing at the end of their line, and many would rather lose their lure than face its vicious fangs. Only those with nerves of steel would attempt to reel in one of these aquatic abominations, though they are often made to regret it.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Coeurlfish

grade 2 skybuilders' garpike<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' garpike<tab>The skybuilders' primary reason for requesting this especially savage variety of garpike is to limit the havoc it wreaks in whatever body of water it inhabits. There is nothing less welcoming to a school of docile freshwater dwellers looking for a new home than a snapping maw of razor-sharp teeth heading in their general direction.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Garpike

grade 2 skybuilders' pirarucu<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' pirarucu<tab>The pirarucu's habit of swallowing the lure whole means that most anglers wait until the beast is well and truly dead before they attempt to retrieve it. There is always the option of leaving it in the fish's belly─but that would be a nasty surprise for the poor soul who has to gut it.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Pirarucu

grade 2 skybuilders' brown bolo<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' brown bolo<tab>While this bizarre creature is known to entangle its prey in a manner similar to its namesake, the grade 2 variety can be used as an actual bolo when thrown. ※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Brown Bolo

grade 2 skybuilders' bitterling<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' bitterlings<tab>Most creatures tend not to enjoy being pulled to their death via a hook to the mouth, but this poor specimen looks especially miserable when caught.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Bitterling

grade 2 skybuilders' caiman<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' caimans<tab>Though the skybuilders are often willing to take in scalekin captured alive, they have specifically requested that any caiman presented be certifiably dead before being brought to the Firmament. Given its resemblance to a wingless dragon, the less sensible members of the populace may fear a second Dragonsong War is upon them.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Caiman

grade 2 skybuilders' cloud cutter<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' cloud cutters<tab>Often caught accidentally by anglers in mid-cast, due to its habit of flying several fulms above the waterline.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Cloud Cutter

grade 2 skybuilders' vampiric tapestry<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' vampiric tapestries<tab>Another species that largely fails to live up to its namesake, especially the “vampiric” part. ※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Vampiric Tapestry

grade 2 skybuilders' tupuxuara<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' tupuxuaras<tab>The word “fishing” usually implies that some sort of aquatic, or at the very least, amphibious creature is the intended prey, though the paraphernalia used by anglers is equally effective for snagging flying scalekin. Whether one would actually want to or not is a separate matter entirely.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Tupuxuara

grade 2 skybuilders' blind manta<tab>grade 2 skybuilders' blind mantas<tab>As this species of manta uses echolocation to find its way around, it can be heard making a series of high-pitched squeals when hoisted out of the water. Many fishers end up feeling sorrow for the poor beast and returning it whence it came, although the more cynically minded suspect it of intentionally wielding a pity-based form of self-defense.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Skybuilders' Blind Manta

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Pterodactyl

pot of carpenter's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of carpenter's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by means that are intriguing─but not quite so intriguing that you would risk finding out what they are. Tastes of sawdust...not that you would know.<tab>Carpenter's Gobbiegoo

pot of blacksmith's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of blacksmith's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by means that are intriguing─but not quite so intriguing that you would risk finding out what they are. Cold to the touch.<tab>Blacksmith's Gobbiegoo

pot of highly viscous blacksmith's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of highly viscous blacksmith's gobbiegoo<tab>This Skysteel tool coating is of a peculiar shiny black, and you cannot shake the feeling that it is somehow gooier than ever before.<tab>Highly Viscous Blacksmith's Gobbiegoo

pot of armorer's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of armorer's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by means that are intriguing─but not quite so intriguing that you would risk finding out what they are. Brittle when spread overthin.<tab>Armorer's Gobbiegoo
pot of highly viscous armorer's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of highly viscous armorer's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating. Now with extra...goo.<tab>Highly Viscous Armorer's Gobbiegoo

pot of goldsmith's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of goldsmith's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by means that are intriguing─but not quite so intriguing that you would risk finding out what they are. Enticingly shiny.<tab>Goldsmith's Gobbiegoo

pot of highly viscous goldsmith's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of highly viscous goldsmith's gobbiegoo<tab>This thick Skysteel tool coating emits fumes that you recall fondly from the gilding process. You also recall said fumes are highly toxic.<tab>Highly Viscous Goldsmith's Gobbiegoo

pot of leatherworker's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of leatherworker's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by means that are intriguing─but not quite so intriguing that you would risk finding out what they are. Known for its delightful aroma─though perhaps leatherworkers are not best positioned to judge.<tab>Leatherworker's Gobbiegoo

pot of highly viscous leatherworker's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of highly viscous leatherworker's gobbiegoo<tab>Even practiced leatherworkers are disgusted by the texture of this Skysteel tool coating─which is really saying something.<tab>Highly Viscous Leatherworker's Gobbiegoo

pot of weaver's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of weaver's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by means that are intriguing─but not quite so intriguing that you would risk finding out what they are. Not a suitable substitute for medicinal salves, no matter how much your fingers ache.<tab>Weaver's Gobbiegoo

pot of highly viscous weaver's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of highly viscous weaver's gobbiegoo<tab>Generally “viscous” is not high on the list of attributes one associates with delicate needlework, but perhaps the frankly alarming amount of goo that Skysteel engineers will soon apply to your needle will change that.<tab>Highly Viscous Weaver's Gobbiegoo
pot of alchemist's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of alchemist's gobbiegoo<tab>A Skysteel tool coating crafted by deeply intriguing means.<tab>Alchemist's Gobbiegoo

pot of highly viscous alchemist's gobbiegoo<tab>pots of highly viscous alchemist's gobbiegoo<tab>“Does the adjective placement here imply that the alchemist in question is particularly viscous?” is a thought that could only come from the addled mind of one steeped in the alchemical arts─which is precisely the reason that no one trusts those people.<tab>Highly Viscous Alchemist's Gobbiegoo

grade 3 skybuilders' thunderbolt sculpin<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' thunderbolt sculpin<tab>Despite the impressive and imposing pattern of a lightning bolt running down its back, this fish gives off no notable electrical discharge, much to the relief of anglers who manage to reel one in.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Thunderbolt Sculpin

grade 3 skybuilders' alligator snapping turtle<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' alligator snapping turtles<tab>To count the number of fishermen who have lost fingers and toes to this savage beast one would need─well, more digits than any of those unfortunate individuals have remaining, to say the least.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Alligator Snapping Turtle

grade 3 skybuilders' bonytongue<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' bonytongues<tab>Notwithstanding its decidedly unflattering moniker, this wavekin cuts a rather striking figure with its vivid red-hued scales, leading some to wonder whatever grudge the naturalist who named it had against the poor creature.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Bonytongue

grade 3 skybuilders' hermit goby<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' hermit gobies<tab>One glance at this unsightly wavekin and any angler will understand why it chooses to spend the majority of its life hidden from view─though recently, some aesthetes have bafflingly come to find beauty in its grotesqueness.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Hermit Goby

grade 3 skybuilders' mudskipper<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' mudskippers<tab>This amphibious fish spends the better part of its time wallowing about in mire and muck, perhaps in vain hope that making itself appear as repulsive as possible will dissuade anglers from wanting to catch it.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Mudskipper

grade 3 skybuilders' steppe bullfrog<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' steppe bullfrogs<tab>While one might indeed wonder what a so-called “steppe” bullfrog is doing amidst the floating isles of the Diadem, one might stop to consider whether the creature in question would ask the same question of you.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Steppe Bullfrog

grade 3 skybuilders' golden loach<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' golden loaches<tab>One is encouraged to take especial care when reeling in this striking specimen so as not to besmirch its pristine appearance─sadly, its tendency to thrash and turn about can make this an all-but-impossible task.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Golden Loach

grade 3 skybuilders' bass<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' bass<tab>Though it is not easily reeled in, many anglers breathe a sigh of relief when assigned this wavekin, if only for its easily-pronounced name. After all, shouting out “Fifteen grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' archaeopteryges submitted for your approval, sir!” and the like can be something of a chore.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Bass

grade 3 skybuilders' cherax<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' cherax<tab>Naturalists particular about nomenclature are quick to note that the plural of “cherax” is, in fact, “cherax,” and not “cheraxes.” More practical-minded anglers are equally quick to note that knowing such trivia will not avail one in avoiding its fearsome pincers.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Cherax

grade 3 skybuilders' marimo<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' marimo<tab>A delight to observe wherever they are encountered, the sight of these green tufts of mossy fluff dancing and darting through the clouds amidst the isles of the Diadem is particularly breathtaking to behold.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Marimo

grade 3 skybuilders' catfish<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' catfish<tab>Some naturalists posit that, unlike its namesake, the catfish derives a degree of pleasure from having its whiskers tickled. Whether it would still appreciate this gesture when performed by the person who plucked the creature unceremoniously from the sky is another question.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Catfish

grade 3 skybuilders' ricefish<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' ricefish<tab>So named because it is native to the rice paddies of the Far East, one might speculate as to why this wavekin has ventured so far from home. One might also ignore such trivialities and simply reel it in, a course of action which undoubtedly would prove more fruitful.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Ricefish

grade 3 skybuilders' scorpionfly<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' scorpionflies<tab>Is it a scorpion, or is it a fly? Actually, it's neither─but rather a volitant species of shrimp that vaguely resembles an amalgamation of the two disparate creatures whose name it bears.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Scorpionfly

grade 3 skybuilders' whiteloom<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' whitelooms<tab>Observing the brilliant, nigh-silken tapestry these wavekin appear to weave as they dance and twirl through the clouds in the Diadem has lent further weight to the arguments of those who claim that its current nomenclature─and not “whiteroom”─is the proper one.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Whiteloom

grade 3 skybuilders' pteranodon<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' pteranodons<tab>One great mystery is how these prehistoric scalekin came to take up residence in the Diadem. A still greater mystery is why procuring them is so vital to the restoration effort.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Pteranodon

grade 3 skybuilders' king's mantle<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' king's mantles<tab>Despite this creature's most impressive moniker─and even more impressive appearance─one is discouraged from actually attempting to wear one, as the slime and stench it exudes make it rather unsuitable as garb, for royalty or otherwise.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' King's Mantle

grade 3 skybuilders' blue medusa<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' blue medusae<tab>Take care when fishing for this spiny creature─though its gaze will not turn you to stone, the poisonous barbs that line its tentacles will have a similarly paralyzing effect.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Blue Medusa

grade 3 skybuilders' gurnard<tab>grade 3 skybuilders' gurnard<tab>It is said that the name of this flying wavekin is derived from the guttural grunting sound it emits as it flies through the sky, an unfortunate trait that rather detracts from its overall elegant visual aspect.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Skybuilders' Gurnard

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' oscar<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' oscars<tab>This strikingly colored wavekin with flowing fins is both beautiful to behold as it is appealing to the appetite─posing quite the dilemma for any angler who is skilled and fortunate enough to reel one in.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Oscar

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' blind manta<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' blind mantas<tab>One might wonder how these eyeless creatures are able to navigate the clouds of the Diadem. While some naturalists posit that heightened tactile senses allow them to feel the winds and avoid collisions with floating rocks and other obstacles, others point out that the scratches observed in some of their bodies suggest that some are more successful at this than others.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Blind Manta

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' mosasaur<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' mosasaurs<tab>Despite being powerful swimmers, these massive and aggressive aquatic scalekin prefer to lie in wait, pouncing on their prey from places unseen and devouring them whole.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Mosasaur

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' storm chaser<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' storm chasers<tab>What is it that compels the storm chaser to forsake calm and welcoming skies for the danger of raging tempests and crackling thunderbolts? Perhaps it is the same as what stirs adventurers to set forth in search of trials and tribulations to overcome.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Storm Chaser

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' archaeopteryx<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' archaeopteryges<tab>This remarkable creature serves as living proof of the relationship between common birds and the massive prehistoric scalekin that ruled both land and sky.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Archaeopteryx

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' wyvern<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' wyverns<tab>Is this an <var 1A 02 /var>actual<var 1A 01 /var> wyvern, or simply a sizable wavekin that bears a remarkable resemblance to its namesake? It is not immediately clear─and neither is why the creature is so vital for the restoration effort. It <var 1A 02 /var>is<var 1A 01 /var> artisanal, though, which doubtless counts for something.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Wyvern

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudshark<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudsharks<tab>It is unclear how this massive, fearsome predator evolved to swim among the clouds rather than the waters preferred by its fellow wavekin, but one thing is certain─less physically imposing denizens of the Diadem doubtless wish it had not.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Cloudshark

grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' helicoprion<tab>grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' helicoprions<tab>These terrifying creatures are noted for their whorls of innumerous razor-sharp teeth, which allow them to shred their prey with remarkable efficiency. It is recommended to ensure the creature is duly dead before admiring these teeth whorls for yourself, lest you share a similarly grisly fate.

※Not included in the fish guide.<tab>Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Helicoprion

hermetic tomestone<tab>hermetic tomestones<tab>While it is a surpassingly small means of storing knowledge, the information deposited on this relic of Allagan society was compressed with heretofore unseen efficiency.
